主要内容: On June 5, 2019, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) adopted new rules and interpretations aimed at enhancing protections for retail investors while preserving their choice and access to investment services. These measures include Regulation Best Interest, which requires broker-dealers to act in the best interest of retail customers when making recommendations. Additionally, the Form CRS Relationship Summary will provide retail investors with clear, easy-to-understand information about their relationship with financial professionals. The SEC also issued interpretations to clarify the fiduciary duty of investment advisers and the 'solely incidental' prong of the broker-dealer exclusion under the Advisers Act. These actions are designed to align legal requirements with investor expectations while maintaining access to a range of products and services at a reasonable cost. The new rules will become effective 60 days after publication in the Federal Register, with a transition period until June 30, 2020. The final regulation, an enhancement from the proposal, requires broker-dealers to consider the costs of recommendations and ensure they are in the retail customer’s best interest. The rules also mandate that broker-dealers establish and enforce written policies to identify and disclose or eliminate conflicts of interest. These policies must mitigate conflicts that could prioritize the firm’s interests over the retail customer’s, prevent material limitations on offerings, and eliminate sales contests and bonuses based on specific securities. Additionally, broker-dealers must comply with Regulation Best Interest by maintaining policies that ensure adherence to the regulation. The SEC also introduced the Form CRS Relationship Summary, a standardized question-and-answer format that provides retail investors with information about services, fees, conflicts of interest, and disciplinary history. The summary promotes comparison and allows for layered disclosure, while also highlighting the SEC’s investor education website, Investor.gov. The rules, forms, and interpretations will be published on the SEC’s website and in the Federal Register, with effectiveness starting 60 days after publication. The SEC has adopted new rules and interpretations aimed at enhancing protections for retail investors in their relationships with financial professionals. These rules require the Commission to prepare, deliver to retail investors, and file a relationship summary. To support firms in complying with these new regulations, the SEC has established an inter-Divisional Standards of Conduct Implementation Committee. This committee includes representatives from various divisions and offices within the SEC, such as the Division of Investment Management, Division of Trading and Markets, and the Office of Compliance Inspections and Examinations. Firms are encouraged to engage with this committee as they plan for implementation. Questions can be sent to IABDQuestions@sec.gov. The new rules include the Final Rule - Regulation Best Interest, Final Rule - Form CRS, Relationship Summary, and Form ADV Amendments, along with Commission Interpretations on the Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers and Broker-Dealer Exclusion.
